headline: Race week handled well: calf tweak on the 28th stopped early and cleared by physio, achilles 0, recovery flat; hold, with the November build starting Monday and the calf gating the return of quality.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 1 November 2026

Shep — Guy Fawkes isn't in the pull yet (only the warm-up runs and strides are), so this is written before the result. Tell me the time, the chest, the calf, and what you took. I'll read it against the 29:12 record and the model's ~17:54 5K on the next turn.

## The week (26 Oct – 1 Nov)

Planned: rest / 8 / 200s / 7 / 6 / 4 / race. Done: rest, 8.0 easy, 200s cut short (7.3 km all in), a rest day (physio), 6.0, 4.7, then the race. About 26 km before race day: a deliberate race-week trough, after 46.8 km last week and 65 the week before.

**28 Oct 200s: the calf.** Felt strong, then on the sixth rep the middle of the left calf tightened and you stopped. Right call: stopping at the first sign is what separates a tweak from a strain. Physio on the 29th ruled out a tear; by Friday you could feel it only slightly, and the strides on Saturday were fine. It is the **calf belly, not the achilles**: achilles has scored 0 every day, and no first-step or desk-chair stiffness is mentioned. But a calf tightening during fast reps is the same load chain, and it came in the first speed work after a 10K. A reason for care when quality returns, not for alarm.

## Recovery

HRV 7-day baseline 35.9 (38.8 two weeks ago), so it has settled lower rather than recovered; RHR baseline 48.7. This morning: HRV 37, RHR 48, sleep 89, status BALANCED. Friday's gate (baseline still sliding, or RHR 51+) did not trip: the baseline is flat and the highest RHR was 50. Garmin ACWR 0.8, acute load below chronic, as a race week should be. Nothing needs excusing.

Worth watching: HRV has sat at 35–36 for two weeks, below September. Flat, not falling. With volume about to rise, this is the number that says whether the build is being absorbed.

## Efficiency and form

Easy running steady at ~4:46–5:00/km, HR 136–141. Weekly efficiency flat (the lower reading this week is slower easy running, not lost fitness). Predictor: 5K 17:54, 10K 37:20, half 1:21:49 (Cheltenham carries 56% of the half weight). VO2max 59 to 58; the predictor flags it, and one point in a taper means little.

## Looking ahead

- **Fission 20 entries open about now and sell out every year.** Enter this week if you want the March rehearsal.
- **The half PB (1:20:46) needs a half in the calendar.** Raise it when the winter block is written; a Feb/March tune-up half fits marathon practice anyway.
- **Asthma:** you planned to raise the 17 Oct cold-air tightness with your GP or asthma nurse after Stroud. That is now. Bring the date, 6–7 °C, last ~3 min of 2x15 threshold, both inhalers taken, settled on stopping.
- **November build starts Monday.** 2–8 Nov ~62 km: Tuesday 12, first 18 km long run with gels, no quality. 9–15 Nov: intervals and tempo return, volume held ~64. 16–22 Nov: quality unchanged, only the long run steps to 20 (~66 km). Volume and intensity never rise together.
- **Calf rule:** the first quality session back (Wed 11 Nov, 4x1 km) is conditional on the calf being silent the week before. Leg gym returns Wednesday with calf and soleus work, graded not heavy, since that is the tissue that just complained. If it nags on the Tuesday, cut to 8 and tell me.

## Recommendation

**Hold.** The week went as designed apart from the calf, which you handled well. Changes are only the horizon extended to 22 Nov, the calf condition, and a provisional 20 km long run in the third week. If today's race leaves the calf sore, say so and week one becomes easy running only.
